label: sec:cp-violation-evidence
html:
Definition of CP violation. CP symmetry enforces perfect mirroring between matter and antimatter. CP violation fundamentally distinguishes them.

Experimental evidence.

Three systems establish CP violation:

  1. Neutral kaons (1964). Cronin and Fitch observed K_L \to \pi^+\pi^- at a rate of \sim 2 \times 10^{-3} [christenson1964].
  2. B mesons (2001). BaBar [aubert2001] and Belle measured CP-violating asymmetries in B^0 \to J/\psi\, K_S, confirming the complex CKM phase \delta_{\mathrm{CKM}}.
  3. D mesons (2019). LHCb measured CP violation in charm decays.

The matter-antimatter asymmetry.

Sakharov required C and CP violation for baryogenesis. The Standard Model CKM phase is quantitatively insufficient to explain the n_B / n_\gamma \sim 6 \times 10^{-10} ratio.

QOU interpretation.

In the complex chirality rotation framework the substrate parameter is complex, q = |q|e^{i\theta}, and the matter-antimatter asymmetry is measured by the discriminant of the two crossing-energy magnitudes,

\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} = \frac{\lVert\mathfrak{E}_+\rVert - \lVert\mathfrak{E}_-\rVert}{\lVert\mathfrak{E}_+\rVert + \lVert\mathfrak{E}_-\rVert}.

The phase does not enter it. Writing the particle's crossing energy as n q and the mirror's as -n/q, per crossing energy on an all-positive braid together with antiparticle crossing reversal, the discriminant of their norms is

\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} = \frac{r^2 - 1}{r^2 + 1}, \qquad r = \lvert q\rvert,

for every \theta. This is an exact identity, not a leading order: \theta is bound on the left-hand side and absent from the right (QOU.Observations.crossingDisc_norm_theta_free, sorry-free). At the substrate anchor \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 0.10396, which coincides with \tanh(\ln r) and with the count-to-signed channel ratio of the n_- = 0 crossing sector.

The asymmetry is therefore supplied by r > 1 — the substrate being deformed at all — and not by a residual phase. Consequently:

  • The observable sector projects \theta \to 0, and an imperfect projection leaves \theta_{\mathrm{res}}; but the discriminant is blind to it.
  • The \mathcal{O}(\theta_{\mathrm{res}}^2) scaling for single-crossing systems (e^-e^+) is refuted — the quantity is independent of \theta at every order, not only at leading order.
  • A geometric origin for the CKM phase does not follow from this discriminant, which carries no phase information.
  • The multi-crossing accumulation \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \sim n_c\theta_{\mathrm{res}} is a statement about composites and is not addressed by the single-crossing-pair identity above. It is neither established nor refuted here.

Quantitative gap — and the correction widens it.

The crossing energy decomposition provides an EM-to-strong ratio of \tanh(\ln r) \approx 0.104. This block previously set \theta_{\mathrm{res}} \sim \tanh(\ln r)\cdot\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \approx 7.5866 \times 10^{-4} and reported an asymmetry of order 10^{-3} matching the kaon \varepsilon \approx 2\times10^{-3}. With the phase removed the framework's value is \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 0.10396, larger by exactly 1/\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \approx 137.04, so the claimed kaon agreement is lost: the ratio is \approx 52 rather than \approx 0.38. The correction is recorded because it is what the identity gives, not because it improves the comparison.

Against the observed baryon-to-photon ratio \eta \approx 6.1\times10^{-10} the framework's asymmetry is too large, by a factor \approx 1.7\times10^{8}. The open object is therefore a suppression f = \eta/\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 5.87\times10^{-9} — an entropy or washout factor — and not a further asymmetry. That search direction is constrained: the bar-odd part of \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}] is free of rank one over its bar-even part, generated by q - q^{-1} (QOU.Observations.BarParityRankOne.isBarOdd_iff, sorry-free), so no second bar-odd shape is available. A ratio of counts is a different kind of quantity from an amplitude.
